title: ai_prompt_shield plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_prompt_shield` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiPromptShieldConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiPromptShieldConfig.description: Plugin: ai_prompt_shield — HTTP-only PII detection and redaction in bare JSON AI prompts. Native gRPC is unsupported (not registered for the Grpc protocol view). Framed gRPC-Web bodies (recognized by the proxy's delimiter-aware gRPC-Web classifier, so application/grpc-webhook+json is ordinary JSON) remain outside the JSON inspection scope and are skipped without decoding. In content/all mode every other POST, PUT, and PATCH is in scope whatever its Content-Type: a JSON media type is declared JSON, and a non-UTF-8 body, a body the strict JSON parser refuses, an oversized body, or a non-UTF-8 charset declaration is refused by reject/redact (400 ai_shield_rejected=non_utf8_body / malformed_json / unsupported_charset, 413 above max_scan_bytes) and recorded by warn; any other or missing Content-Type is sniffed and held to the same rules whenever the body may be a JSON document (strict JSON, a BOM, UTF-16/UTF-32, a leading comment, or a JSON root scalar), while text and binary uploads are left alone. Enforcing actions claim encoded sniffed bodies so the representation gate decodes them first. Inspection is scoped to POST/PUT/PATCH (mcp_arguments: POST) on every hook, including the request-body transform, so a co-located body plugin that forces buffering cannot extend redaction to another method. Every in-scope request — scope decided again from the final headers, so a header rewrite cannot carry a request past it — is re-decided in on_final_request_body over the exact backend-visible body after all request-body transforms; reject and warn re-decide there and redact fails closed, because that hook cannot rewrite wire bytes.

patterns.description: Built-in patterns: ssn, credit_card, email, phone_us, api_key, aws_key, ip_address, iban. Each name at most once.

custom_patterns.description: Custom {name, regex} patterns. Each entry accepts exactly these two members; an unknown member is fatal at construction, like an unknown top-level field. `regex` must not match the empty string — a zero-width rule would insert the redaction placeholder at every position — and `name` is bounded (maxLength, in characters) because it is substituted into redaction_placeholder. At most 256 entries. Match enumeration is work-bounded: each walk over a custom pattern's matches is charged, per match, up to the match start plus the pattern's longest possible match (the rest of the string when unbounded), against 256 times the scanned string's length (4 MiB floor); exhaustion fails closed (redaction returns 413 redaction_budget_exceeded, detection counts the pattern as matched).

scan_fields.description: Which parts of the request to scan. 'mcp_arguments' scans only params.arguments of MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests (a singleton or every tools/call member of a batch), accepts the media types mcp_gateway admits (application/json, application/json-rpc, +json, or no Content-Type), and refuses a body with duplicate member names under reject/redact (400, ai_shield_rejected=ambiguous_json). 'content' scans LLM prompt fields only: chat messages[].content plus top-level prompt, input, instructions, system, inputText, message, preamble, and inputs (completions/responses/embeddings/Anthropic-system/Bedrock-Titan/Cohere-v1/HuggingFace-TGI shapes), Google Gemini contents[].parts[].text and systemInstruction/system_instruction parts, Cohere chat_history[].message, Google Vertex legacy predict instances[].prompt, Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolResult content and guardContent text, Anthropic tool_result block content, tool-call arguments replayed in the history (OpenAI messages[].tool_calls[].function.arguments and function_call.arguments, Responses input[] function_call arguments, Anthropic tool_use/server_tool_use/mcp_tool_use input, Bedrock Converse toolUse.input, Gemini parts[].functionCall.args), and Azure On Your Data role_information — including content blocks that carry no type discriminator (Bedrock Converse) and matches split across adjacent text parts. Detection and redaction cover the same field set. 'all' scans the entire request body recursively while exempting only top-level structural scalar values such as model/id/role and numeric tuning parameters; nested occurrences remain scannable. Use 'all' for request shapes that carry prompt text in non-standard fields.

exclude_roles.description: Message roles to skip scanning. Applies to scan_fields: content ONLY — scan_fields: all deliberately scans every value in the body regardless of role, so a role exemption does not preserve a message there. In content mode it filters messages[].role, Gemini contents[].role, and Cohere chat_history[].role (matched case-insensitively, since Cohere spells roles USER/CHATBOT/SYSTEM/TOOL); the value 'system' additionally suppresses the top-level system field, the Cohere preamble, and the Gemini system instruction. Provider inputs that carry no role, such as an OpenAI Responses function_call_output item, are never suppressed.

redaction_placeholder.description: Template for redacted text. `{type}` is substituted with the matched pattern name; the RENDERED result must be at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, since every match re-emits it. Redaction output is additionally charged against a per-request growth allowance of four times the request body size (minimum 65536, maximum 67108864 bytes), measured on the JSON-escaped form, with live intermediate buffers bounded by the same allowance; an expanding policy that exhausts it fails the request closed with 413 rather than forwarding a partially redacted body.

max_scan_bytes.description: Maximum body size to scan; enforcing actions reject larger bodies instead of bypassing inspection. Hard ceiling 67108864 (64 MiB). A mathematically integral value is accepted however it is spelled (1024 and 1024.0 alike); a fractional, negative, zero, or out-of-range value is rejected at construction rather than truncated.
